launches.body:
Hi! We are Lucas and Paul, cofounders of Tire Swing: the AI compliance platform for Affordable Housing.

<https://youtu.be/x4qyhXXz38I>

## **The Problem**

Every Affordable Housing move-in and recertification requires applicant income verification and a strict eligibility review. In addition to the high labor costs and regulatory burden, delays in reviewing applications and thoroughly screening applicants can cause weeks of lost rental revenue.

Lost revenue on a single move-in can accumulate to thousands of dollars, and penalties for non-compliance can cost millions in credit recaptures and fines.

## **The Solution**

Tire Swing uses AI to bring compliance expertise to the point of leasing. It turns weeks of reviews and approvals into a minutes-long process. The platform:

* **Reviews evidence as it is collected.** Tire Swing processes documentation in minutes, allowing problems to be addressed before the applicant leaves the office.
* **Performs the eligibility analysis.** It calculates household income, applies all applicable property, state, and program eligibility rules, and links every finding to its supporting evidence.
* **Automates certification compliance.** Tire Swing flags missing, inconsistent, or incorrect information with steps to resolve the problem from a library of thousands of deterministic and AI driven compliance checks.

**Tire Swing means faster move-ins and recertifications, reduced consulting budget, and more consistent, audit-ready files.** 

## **Looking ahead**

We believe Affordable Housing is the first application of a much larger needs-based eligibility opportunity. Federal, state, and local governments distribute more than $1.5 trillion annually through needs-based programs including Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, utility assistance, and tax credits.

These programs share a common underlying workflow: collect documents, convert them into structured facts, apply eligibility rules, and resolve missing or contradictory information.  The administration costs for these services are approximately $20B annually.

## **The Team**

Tire Swing is founded by Paul and Lucas, college friends and Princeton computer science graduates. Prior to founding Tire Swing, Lucas worked as a software engineer at Instacart and Capital One, and Paul worked as a cybersecurity consultant at Stroz Friedberg.

name: Rodeo Robotics
long_description:
Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time.

Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention.

They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns.

Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles.

Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.
one_liner: Robots for vehicle maintenance.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Roma is the to-do list that does itself. It's the original productivity tool reinvented. The task list you already keep, remade so the tasks actually get done.

<https://youtu.be/6bEw1OBRTkU>

### The original

From pen and paper to apps on a phone, the to-do list has stood the test of time. It's the original productivity tool, and the one tool everyone has used at least once.

You can't say that about many things, especially as technology advances. But whether you have one task or seventeen, there's a to-do list in your head, in your pocket, or on your desk right now.

Since the beginning, all to-do lists have made the same promise: write the task down so you can stop worrying about it. The catch is that you always have to come back and do it yourself. So the tasks pile up.

### The problem

When AI became smart enough to actually help you get things done, we did what a lot of people did and built our own agents. It was hard. It took forever. Even when it worked, it didn't work the way we wanted. 

Then the AI Assistants arrived, promising to handle things for you. People love them. That's the clearest sign the demand is there.

But the work never stay put. It lives in one chat, then another, then an inbox, then a doc somewhere. Instead of doing the work, you're tracking the work down.

### Reinventing the to-do list

That's why we're playing the long game and not building another assistant. We're reinventing the original productivity tool: the to-do list.

**Roma is the to-do list that does itself.** 

That sounds possible with AI, but it's really hard to get right. You have to be able to add a task for anything and the system has to figure out what you meant, get to work on multiple things in the background, sort it into the right project, and surface it at exactly the right time. 

So that's where we spent most of our time building Roma. Underneath Roma is a harness built to take a task from idea to execution. And on top, it feels as simple and light as the to-do list that you're used to. 

### What it feels like

Roma gets real tasks done. But what you notice first is what it does to your mind. You realize you haven't thought about that one task in hours, because it's being handled. You walk into a meeting prepared. You close your laptop with a clear head.

### Why us

We're Jan, Tobi, and Cody. Jan previously built Loom (YC W12, acquired by Dropbox), and Tobi built Senic (YC S13, acquired by Gira). 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117892&key=user_uploads/24212/d1545e35-9497-4e2f-a4f9-34f6420684e6)

### Where this goes

We're only scratching the surface of what Roma can do. As Roma takes on more of your work, the to-do list becomes the place you hand off everything. 

We're going to connect with the apps and assistants you're already using. So whatever you're working on, Roma becomes the center of how it gets done. 

We're only scratching the surface of what Roma can do, and we can't wait to hear what you think.\

We're very excited to hear what you all think!

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

**TL;DR: Veltha is an AI-native TPA for workers' compensation. TPAs process claims for insurance providers, and our AI owns this service end to end. An adjuster only reviews the decision, work that used to take 6 hours now takes 10 minutes - with better outcomes.**

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

TPAs deliver terrible service across the board. We have yet to find a carrier or employer that is happy with theirs. The misalignment is structural: TPAs make most of their profit on fees layered on top of claims handling, so quality of the core service barely affects their bottom line. So we decided to deliver the service ourselves.

**What we built**

Veltha runs the whole claim file end to end:

* **Triage.** Reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection.** Checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review.** Applies the governing laws and produces a determination where every output is tied to a source and a specific regulatory rule.

Our licensed adjusters review and sign every decision. One adjuster on Veltha handles 4x the caseload of a traditional adjuster with better and quicker outcomes.

Veltha is an AI claims adjuster that runs the whole file end to end:

* **Gap detection** - checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.

launches.body:
## **TLDR**

Neomatter is the operating system for in-house legal teams. It plugs into the places your company already works (email, Slack, Salesforce, etc) and picks up legal requests as they come in. When someone sends legal a contract or a question, the work is already done before a lawyer opens it, ready to review and approve.\
\
<https://youtu.be/delvI16C41E>

## **The problem**

Every part of your company runs through legal.

Sales needs contracts signed. HR needs employment agreements. Finance needs board approvals. And every department has legal questions.

But legal teams spend a lot of their time on repetitive work: reviewing the same terms, searching for old agreements, answering familiar questions, and chasing information.

The software tools haven't solved this. One tool manages contracts, another handles requests, and another tracks approvals. Lawyers still have to piece the work together themselves.

And when teams reach capacity, companies hire more lawyers or send work to expensive outside firms.

## **What we’re building**

Neomatter takes a request from start to finish. It gathers context, reviews documents, checks the company’s policies and precedents, and prepares the work for approval.

## **How it works**

Neomatter monitors the places legal requests already come through (email, Slack, teams, Salesforce, and more) and automatically triages requests to the right lawyer. Nobody has to tag anything or learn a new tool.

Then it does the work. It reads everything, does the redlines, checks it against your team’s playbooks, drafts the reply, and waits for your decision. By the time you know the matter exists, 90% of the work has already been done. The lawyer opens finished work, checks the sources, writes any edits, and makes the decision.

And it can handle anything. Commercial work, employment work, corporate work, a “can I do this?” question, or anything else a legal team receives. Neomatter does it all.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122248&key=user_uploads/1633544/eecfd55b-a702-4725-b7b3-3baed9d62b2f)

We’re Luke & Luke. We dropped out of university to move to San Francisco.

We believe AI has fundamentally changed how much work one person can do. After speaking with over 200 in-house legal teams, we realized AI can completely change the way lawyers work.

We’re building Neomatter to make that happen.

name: herdr
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

Rhem was designed with older adults in mind, but it’s for anyone who wants help getting things done and staying on top of their health.**

## 

## The Problem

**At some point, you start paying attention to your parents differently.**

Maybe there was a scare. Maybe Mom missed an appointment. Maybe Dad sounds more tired. Or maybe nothing happened at all. You just start wondering whether everything is as fine as they say.

If you don’t live with them, you mostly get snapshots: a call, a text, a FaceTime.

**You don’t see the full day.**

You don’t know if routines are slipping, something is getting harder, or a small change is becoming a pattern.

**We learned this the hard way with my grandmother.**

Before her stroke, she was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself.

The signs were there. But my dad had a newborn and a full-time job. My grandfather was working too. Everyone cared, but no one saw the whole picture.

**We each saw pieces. No one put them together until something much bigger happened.**

## **How it works for your parents**

Rhem lives in the home and becomes the easiest way for your parent to get things done and keep track of their health.

They just need to say:

“Remind me after dinner.”

“When is my appointment?”

“Order our usual groceries.”

“Tell Jacob I need a ride tomorrow.”

Rhem can browse websites, make calls, manage reminders, answer questions, place supported orders, and follow up.

**If it doesn’t require a pair of hands, Rhem can probably handle it.**

They can also take supported wellness readings on Rhem, keep track of routines, and see how things change over time.

When something needs you, **Rhem brings you into the loop through the rhem connect app.** You can answer a question, add context, or help finish the task. **Help Rhem once, and it remembers how to do it next time.**

## **How it works for families**

Your parent gets an assistant. **You get a clearer picture of how they’re doing.**

The Rhem app brings together health readings, routines, requests, completed tasks, and alerts. You can see what changed, what Rhem handled, and when you’re needed.

From anywhere, you can send reminders, leave voice messages, ask Rhem to check in, talk to your parent, or ask about information they’ve shared.

Over time, Rhem helps you spot patterns. **One bad night may mean nothing. A month of worse sleep, missed appointments, and changes in routine is something you want to know about.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/c7652236-3ca9-40a0-9ea8-d1e2160852fc)

## **Why we built Rhem**

**We’re a father-and-son team, and our family spent nearly two decades caring for loved ones at home.**

Before my grandmother had a stroke, there were signs that something was changing. She was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself. We all noticed pieces of it, but nobody had the full picture until much later.

My aunt had a different problem. A brain tumor left her with limited mobility, so a lot of everyday things depended on someone else being available. Making a call. Looking something up. Ordering something. Figuring out what needed to happen next.

A lot of the time, she didn’t need someone physically next to her. She needed someone who could help her get things done.

That’s where Rhem came from.

**We wanted something that could notice when things were changing, help with the everyday stuff, and bring family in when they were actually needed.**

The goal is simple: give our parents more independence, while letting us spend more time being their family instead of managing everything around them.

name: Munito AI
long_description:
Munito is an open-model inference provider for Europe, private by default. Its API lets users choose their models and keep inference and storage in the EU.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
I led inference at Mistral AI, where my team built its API and inference products, and I built Le Chat's Deep Research. Before that, I spent five years at Airbnb, where I built Hosting Services from scratch and grew it to become a global product.

At Mistral, we built everything in-house, because no independent European provider could handle our scale. I kept seeing the same thing: in Europe, inference is a side product. Cloud providers sell it next to their VMs, and model labs sell it for their own models. At the same time, open models became really good.

This is why I started Munito: the best open models, run in Europe, behind an API you already know how to use.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Companies in Europe want to use the best open models at scale, but they also need privacy and control over where their data is processed. Today it's hard to get both. Most large providers are not European, and EU processing is quite often an extra option instead of the default. There are few European providers, and many of them can't handle real scale.

And this problem grows every month. More and more sensitive data goes through AI models in products, agents and internal tools. Users and regulators ask where it's processed and stored, and companies don't want their AI to depend on one cloud or one model lab.

I saw this from inside at Mistral, where we had to build everything in-house. Munito gives companies open models at scale, with inference and storage in the EU and privacy by default: no data retention, no training on their data. Sovereignty, without running your own GPUs.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
I believe that open and independent intelligence, both models and inference, is key to economic growth and prosperity in the world and the region.

If Munito succeeds, anyone building with AI can run the best open models privately, in the region they choose, without depending on one cloud or one model lab. Munito rents GPUs across many vetted data centers and clouds, and we’re building a self-improving inference stack, so running open models gets faster and cheaper over time.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Food distributors still receive orders from old-school restaurants via text, phone and handwritten notes, and a rep manually retypes every one into a legacy ERP. Asakana reads those messages and does the entry automatically. Restaurants and reps keep working the way they do today. In production at a US food distributor.

<https://youtu.be/XONUcUsuxSY>

**The problem**

A food distributor runs on messages. Restaurants order by text, phone, WhatsApp, a photo of a handwritten note, often not in English. They report an incorrect, short, or damaged delivery the same way. A rep or an admin staff member reads every one of those messages and enters it by hand into an ERP or spreadsheet: the order, the return, the credit memo.

One of our customers receives about 60 orders a day this way, some over 75 lines. A sales rep reads each one, works out which of 10 salmon items "salmon" means, and types it into the ERP line by line. Then the credit requests from yesterday's deliveries, each one a return and a credit note typed in by hand. Reps there spend about 30% of their day on this.

Apps and portals tried to replace this manual work, but old school restaurants and distributor’s sales reps never learned them, so the retyping remained. The US has more than 27,000 food distributors and their 100,000 sales reps and back-office staff suffer from painful manual work like this.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122477&key=user_uploads/2103989/75737558-db33-4f61-b265-2230e25c9ef6)

**What Asakana does**

Asakana does the manual work so reps can focus on selling. Restaurants and reps keep working the way they do today. Three steps, the same for every workflow:

* Read messy information: spreadsheets, PDFs, handwritten notes, and messages, down to the photo of the handwritten invoice a driver brings back from a delivery.
* Understand your business: customer habits, product shorthand, and unwritten rules. "Same as last Friday" is order SO-78211. "AC" means albacore tuna. Salmon is always skin-on.
* Connect to your systems: work directly with your existing ERP and tools.

Anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. The rep gets one email notification per task: what was entered and anything to keep an eye on.

Workflows we automate this way:

* Order entry
* Credit memos and returns
* Upsell suggestions
* Cutoff reminders
* Past-due collections
* PO creation
* New customer discovery

Chinese, Korean, Spanish, Japanese: read the way they were written, with the shorthand and nuance of each language, and matched to the item in the English catalog.

Anything that moves by hand from a message into a system or a spreadsheet, we automate.

**The team**

We're Yudai and Ben. Yudai was a fisherman and a seafood distributor (Mitsubishi Corporation), where he did this manual work himself, then at McKinsey transformed companies that still ran on it. Ben spent 8 years at Google as a senior AI research engineer on Project Mariner and Gemini.

**We’re your cracked AI training team, on demand.** We partner with your company, build your in-house model training capabilities, and leave behind Bryel Foundry, our software that makes model development and continual improvement 10x simpler. Think of it as your in-house AI lab. We’ve trained models for Apple, Framer, and F500s.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LsVUbDIG2RY>

## Problem

**When you train a model for everyone, you train it for no one.** 

Frontier models are incredibly capable generalists, but they fall short on the specifics. So teams build harnesses to work around the edges and cover the gaps: more prompting, more harness infra, more retries, and stricter evals.

Eventually, quality plateaus. We’ve met many teams that are buried in harness work, layering on more and more infrastructure and patches to keep things working. That’s where model training is worth a serious look. With recent advancements in the open-source ecosystem and post-training methods, a few thousand good examples can produce a model that beats frontier APIs on your task, and it’s cheaper to run and deployable on-prem.

The challenge has always been that training is slow, expensive, experimental, and requires specialized knowledge. That’s where we help.

## Solution

We forward deploy into your company, to help you set up your AI model training capabilities end-to-end, and hand off software to help you maintain and continually improve your AI models. Our product, the Bryel Foundry, has been built from everything we learned doing this by hand, many times over.

launches.tagline: Turning your designs into precision metal parts in days
launches.body:
👋 **Hey Everyone!** I’m Naman. My best friend Shubh and I are building **Antropi Robotics**.

**We make inspected CNC parts for hardware teams.** Our first factory is live and already shipping parts to customers with **lead times under 7 days**.

**Our goal:** a network of autonomous factories across the US, making and delivering parts locally in as little as 24 hours.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V4Ll5DZSP0I>

## ⚙️ Problem

Before starting Antropi, I spent six months running my dad’s CNC machining business in India. The biggest lesson was simple: **automating the machine is not the same as automating the factory.**

A CNC machine can cut automatically. But someone still has to plan the job, load the machine, inspect the part, and decide what to do when something goes wrong.

For hardware teams, this becomes a familiar cycle. Prepare drawings. Request quotes. Go back and forth on manufacturing details. Wait for a production slot. Wait for the parts.

**Every week spent waiting is a design iteration you don’t get before your next demo.**

Adding a robot to load the machine fixes one step. It does not tell the factory whether the part is correct, or what should happen next.

## 🤖 Solution

We’re building **dark factories: autonomous factories designed to run 24/7.** Our Factory OS connects job planning, CNC machines, robots, and inspection into one system.

Software turns CAD into machining programs and checks them in simulation, with an engineer approving them before production.

Robots load and unload. Machines cut. **Every part is inspected.**

Inspection feeds back into production, so the system can make supported corrections or stop the machine before a problem repeats.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/275935ea-e97d-40e7-b0fa-cc9d04977486)

For you, it’s simple: upload your CAD, confirm your requirements, and receive inspected parts with an inspection report.

**You buy parts. We handle the factory.**

We’re also building agent ordering through our MCP server and a **Rush option** for priority production.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/c7d0124b-0e12-4a10-b4ca-322ecac60205)


## 🌎 Vision

**One factory is the start. The network is the point.**

Our long-term plan is hundreds, eventually thousands, of microfactories across the US, close to the teams building hardware. The same Factory OS will coordinate production across the network.

Autonomy removes waiting inside the factory. Local production puts the finished part closer to you.

The target: **American-made precision at China-competitive prices**, with local delivery in as little as 24 hours for supported parts.

Shenzhen-like speed, without needing to build in Shenzhen.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/e012541d-ba88-4809-9423-a1935c878aec)


## 🛠️ We’ve spent nine years getting hardware built.

Shubh and I met in college in 2017. We both studied computer science, built Mars rovers together, and competed internationally. We also spent plenty of days in CNC shops waiting for parts.

Before running my dad’s business, I was the first employee and Chief of Staff at Accio Robotics, a warehouse automation company in India, participating in its journey from the first product through scaling and acquisition.

Shubh completed his Master’s in Robotics at the University of Pennsylvania, working with robotic manipulators. After his master’s, we started Antropi.

We have experienced this problem as the people waiting for parts and as the people responsible for making them.

**Now we’re building the factories we wish we’d had.**

## 🙌 Ask

**Need CNC parts?** Send us your most challenging part and we’ll get it done. 

👉 [www.antropi.shop](http://antropi.shop)

**Know a team scaling production?** We’d appreciate introductions to hardware or procurement teams at Series B+ companies in computing infrastructure, robotics, medical devices, and energy.

We’re happy to start with one part and earn the next order.

**Naman & Shubh**

Antropi Robotics

launches.body:
**TL;DR - You can stop copy/pasting messages between agents now**

Soon, agents will outnumber people on the internet. We think they should be able to find each other, talk to each other, and work together.

Today, even agents working on the same project depend on humans to connect them. My agent needs something from your agent, so the message takes this route:

My agent → **me → you** → your agent.

Every person on the team can have agents producing work faster, while the team still waits on people to pass questions, context, and updates between them. We’re all the bottleneck!

We built Agent Relay to fix that.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124128&key=user_uploads/50118/7832a56a-13b4-49e3-a610-bf9dfbab0b49)

**How it works**

Agent Relay works inside the tools you already use, like the Codex Mac app, Claude in the terminal or even Conductor. Start your sessions as usual, and then choose which agents they can talk to. Relay runs in the background, delivering messages between them.

Before Relay, handing off work meant having my agent write up a summary, pasting it to Khaliq in Slack, and him pasting it into his agent. Now my agent just asks his. It can read his session to see what he changed and why, ask follow-up questions, and get pinged the moment his work is ready.

We don’t have to carry messages between them, and everyone can keep using their preferred tools.

Shared, searchable session history lets agents catch up on what their teammates did and why, even after those sessions have ended.

Agent Relay is [open source](https://github.com/agentworkforce/relay). You can self-host it or if you prefer to not to spend your days managing difficult infrastructure you can use our hosted cloud.

We’re building **Energy Superintelligence: swarms of coordinated AI agents to operate energy infrastructure and data centers, carrying out work across entire organizations.**

Energy is one of the bottlenecks to scaling intelligence. Our vision is agents coordinating humans and other agents to operate, maintain, and build energy infrastructure worldwide, with applications extending to data centers.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE>

We reached out to roughly 5,000 people in energy and had over 400 conversations. The same problem kept appearing: people were manually connecting fragmented data, investigating faults, and coordinating work across departments.

Our engineers work inside energy companies to map their data, workflows, responsibilities, and operating procedures. We combine that knowledge with an energy-specific ontology, giving specialized agents a shared understanding of the business and procedures they can follow. We see the same opportunity in data center operations: connecting equipment, maintenance procedures, suppliers, and on-site teams so agents can coordinate real work.

Hello world, we’re [Irene](https://www.linkedin.com/in/irene-grace-karot-polson/) & [Sahith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sahith-reddy-chada/), co-founders of [Deploy](https://deployrobotics.co/)!\
\
**TL;DR:** Deploy puts generalist robots, aka humanoid arms, to work in real businesses as a service. You pay for the work getting done (packing, kitting, returns, manufacturing, data center maintenance), not the robot.

<https://youtu.be/cPinFIhI7b8>

**Problem:** \
The world was full of physical tasks no technology could automate till now. Generalist robot models can finally handle the messy, variable work that traditional automation never could: mixed orders, returns, tasks that change every day.

But a capable model isn't the same as a robot reliably doing the job on your floor. Most robotics projects stall in the gap between a good demo and a shift that runs 24/7. 

**Solution:** \
Deploy closes that gap. We’re the generalist robot deployment company. We turn generalist robots into reliable workers, and our customers pay for completed work, not the robot.

**How it works:** \
→ We break each new task into a sequence of steps and track progress in real time\
→ The system knows what's done, what's next, and when a robot needs help\
→ Every human intervention becomes training data, so the robots get better the longer they run

**The backstory**\
[Irene](https://www.linkedin.com/in/irene-grace-karot-polson/) and [Sahith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sahith-reddy-chada/) have been building robots for over a decade, from opposite ends of the stack. Sahith built robot models at Honda Research Institute. Irene deployed autonomous vehicles in safety-critical airport environments. We kept hitting the same wall: deployment. Deploying across different robots and different models is fundamentally the same problem. If it’s one problem, one platform can solve it. So we’re building Deploy.

**TL;DR: We're 40-50% faster than existing cloud providers in serving frontier robot AI models, e.g. DreamZero, MolmoAct2.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVqvJFBRcd0>

\[1x speed, autonomous\]

DSL is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. We let you deploy physical AI without needing expensive local GPUs.

Robot foundation models are growing more and more computationally expensive. The latest frontier of robotics no longer fits feasibly on local GPUs. Compute costs keep soaring amidst a global LPDDR shortage; NVIDIA just doubled the prices of Jetsons in July.

**We're taking a contrarian bet that the future is moving inference _off the robot_ and _into the cloud._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/4ca20fc9-00a8-4043-bc43-d51b8b5d0cbf)

How do we do this? We work across the full stack of robot inference to push latency down:

* Model-level architectural adjustments for faster inference
* Kernel-level optimizations to maximally leverage server-grade GPUs
* Network-level optimizations for fast and reliable transport over the cloud
* Region-specific compute allocation to ensure the shortest physical distance between the servers and our customers' robots

These optimizations enable us to be **8% faster** than NVIDIA's implementation **at half the GPU count** (320ms vs 350ms, for DreamZero 14B).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/69393040-ca17-41cd-a1fb-cd5d70176921)

Furthermore, something we noticed for robotics companies with fast R&D cycles was that their GPUs had long idle periods with concentrated bursts of inference traffic. We're one of the first companies in the world to offer on-demand pricing for physical AI inference, giving users more flexibility with the cost.

We're already working closely with a range of early partners across deployment, research and evaluation. In full FDE spirit, we collaborate with our customers to custom-fit inference stacks that address their unique deployment challenges. We help you get your robot AI to deployment faster.

Our mission is to democratize access to frontier physical intelligence, and we believe cloud is the way forward. You can read our thesis here:

Experiments are slow, expensive, and most of the information they could yield is wasted. The pharmaceutical industry alone performed **$126B of U.S. R&D in 2023**.\

Halmos runs unbounded research by coordinating hundreds of AI agents, checks the logical consistency of their reasoning, and revisits arguments that fail validation before presenting conclusions to your team.\

We start by designing experiments. Hey YC! We’re Koosha and Anmol, the founders of Resin. We’re building an AI-native PCB design tool that helps engineers turn ideas into working electronics faster and more reliably.

**Demo: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JByTuaHHHGg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JByTuaHHHGg)**

Mandatory GIF:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120163&key=user_uploads/501763/ddae1ba4-75e5-43a7-9a30-fe4fa392848f)

**Problem we’re solving**

* **PCB design is slow and manual:** Engineers can spend weeks reading datasheets, finding components, drawing schematics, and routing connections on traditional design tools. 
* **Design mistakes are expensive:** A design error that only gets surfaced _after_ fabrication can require redesigning and manufacturing the board again, adding weeks/months of delay and cost.
* **Requires expertise:** Good board design takes years of experience to master, so many smaller companies can't do it in-house. Resin makes it accessible to experts and non-experts (including hobbyists) alike.

**How Resin solves this problem**

Resin brings AI into a complete ECAD workspace to increase engineering velocity & design reliability:

* **Draft and review schematics:** Describe your requirements. Resin researches parts, drafts schematics, and documents its design decisions. It also reviews existing designs to help catch mistakes before manufacturing.
* **Find or generate any part:** Tell Resin which component you need. It searches millions of parts, analyzes them deeply and generates accurate symbols and footprints.
* **Route boards:** Connect selected signals or your whole board with our proprietary routing engine. We’re especially excited about this one!
* **In the cloud and collaborative:** Resin runs fully in the cloud, and allows seamless collaboration across multiple users!
* **Prepare for manufacturing:** Check component pricing and availability, manage your bill of materials, and export manufacturing files.
* **Stay in control:** Resin is a complete EDA workspace with full schematic, PCB tooling (**and not a mere chatbot!**). Users can delegate entire workflows to AI or get hands-on with individual components, connections, and traces. Every AI change is editable and auditable.
* **Bring existing work into Resin:** We have full support for project & library imports from Altium & KiCad so you can continue existing projects in Resin! There are more integrations on the way!
* **MCP compatible:** Work from Claude Code, Codex, etc.

**Team**

We’ve been long time friends — we met in college where we studied Engineering Physics together! Koosha has tons of electronics and hardware experience, having designed very complex hardware at Bosch, Kodak, IHS. Anmol mostly recently led the FDE team at [you.com](http://you.com) and was an early member at various successful AI startups.

**Know someone who designs electronics? We’d love intros** to other founders, electrical engineers, hardware leads whether they’re building robots, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment, or consumer products.

launches.title: Particularity: AI investigators for government regulators
launches.tagline: AI agents that catch consumer protection violations before anyone complains
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're Kavin and Chris.

**TL;DR:** Particularity gives federal, state, and city consumer protection agencies AI agents that check live websites for violations like junk fees, subscription traps, and deceptive ads and turn what they find into court-ready evidence.

<https://youtu.be/f6qVdEjYR9Y>

**What enforcement looks like today**

Chris and I found ourselves frustrated by the deluge of undisclosed advertising on social media (which violates FTC guidelines) and started thinking,“How does a government agency capture the true scope of illicit activity at scale?”

That question led us to find that most consumer protection regulation today still starts with a complaint. Investigators work through an inbox that never empties, while millions of websites change every day. Most people who are harmed never file at all. 

The result is ad hoc enforcement: few companies get caught and often years later. When breaking the rules rarely costs anything, competition stops being about who builds the better product and starts being about who's willing to cheat.

**What Particularity does**

\- **Uncover.** Agents check live websites the way a consumer would. Does the advertised price match checkout? Can you actually cancel online? Every step is captured, timestamped, and hashed.

\- **Investigate.** Every complaint gets a first-pass investigation within the same minute, matched against evidence already on file.

\- **Act.** Findings map to the elements of the law, so staff can move straight to a warning letter or enforcement action.

**About us**

Kavin worked at a causal inference startup and on consumer protection and capital markets at the Senate Banking Committee. Chris built security and compliance infrastructure at AWS, including services for the EU Sovereign Cloud. \
\
**If you’re a regulator, please reach out!**

We’re interested in talking to consumer protection staff at state AG offices, large city consumer affairs departments, and state agencies. We’d also love to talk to any former FTC or CFPB folks and others generally in the consumer protection space.

launches.tagline: Native predicts what you should post, and then runs it across your socials and ads.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋

Ben, Håkon and Trond here, founders of Native (YC F26). 

Today we're introducing Norn, a model that predicts which marketing ideas are outliers, before the content is made. We call it artificial intuition, and have our first model live in Native helping over 2000 companies run their marketing. By dogfooding we've reached $2M ARR within our first 6 months.

<https://youtu.be/YTpaKxp1NOs>

**The problem**

AI has made it much easier to produce text, images and video. But you still have to decide what’s worth saying, which angle fits your brand and what your audience might care about.

Producing more content doesn’t answer those questions. It just produces more noise.

Our bet: knowing what to say becomes more valuable as creating it gets cheaper.

**How Norn works**

Just type in your website. Native gathers your business and brand context, and Norn ranks ideas using four signals:

* Brand personality: your voice, positioning and style
* Social performance: what happened after content was published
* Trends: what people are paying attention to
* Taste: which ideas you approve, rewrite or reject

Norn’s output is an idea: the point to make, the angle and the format. Native uses frontier models to turn it into images, video, ad creatives and social posts. You review the results, and Native handles scheduling and publishing.

The original idea, your feedback and the published result become part of the learning loop.

**Already live**

More than 2,000 businesses use Native, and Norn v1 is already working inside it.

That gives us something useful to build on: feedback from the whole creative process, from the first suggestion to what happens after publishing.

**Why us**

Ben comes from YouTube and agency work, with 15 years in content and marketing. Trond built a marketing agency and founded a music festival. Håkon built machine learning models for visual imagery and brings the AI and engineering background.

Between us, we’ve spent years creating content and building the software behind it. Native brings those experiences together.

**Next: the Norn API**

We’re developing an API so other products can ask for ranked ideas before creating content: a marketing tool, an agency workflow or an AI agent deciding what to make next. Like Jev for marketing.

In the video, we explain the model and where we want to take it.

**Our ask**

If you’re building a product that creates content, join the Norn API waitlist and tell us what you’d build: <https://native.no/norn>

launches.body:
Hey everyone! I'm [Vedant Gaur](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vedantgaur/) from [Latent](https://runlatent.ai/).

**TL;DR: Latent catches your AI's wrong answers before your users see them. It reads signals inside the model while it answers, scores every response, and stops the ones about to be wrong. It works with any model and costs over 500x less than an LLM judge.**

Website: [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai)\
Start free: [app.runlatent.ai](http://app.runlatent.ai)

[Demo](https://youtu.be/Dd8cez0CIDY)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123748&key=user_uploads/1788540/af18344d-59fb-4a63-9f84-65e38f95a216)

**The Problem:**

AI fails quietly. A model gives a fluent, confident answer that's wrong: the wrong dosage, a refund policy that doesn't exist, a clause that isn't in the contract. Latency is fine, the dashboard is green, and the model passed last week's evals. You find out when a customer does.

The usual fix is a second LLM that re-reads the output. That's slow and expensive, so most teams only check a sample, and everything outside it ships unchecked. In healthcare, finance, insurance, and legal, that gap is what keeps AI out of production.

**What We're Doing:**

**1. Reading the model while it answers**\
Latent scores every answer from signals inside the model. On self-hosted models, a read-only hook reads the hidden state as tokens are generated, with no added latency. On API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, a lightweight reader model scores each answer in milliseconds.

**2. Stopping wrong answers before anyone sees them**\
You decide what happens per model: hold the answer and show a fallback, re-ask a stronger model, or send it to a review queue with the reason attached. About 95% of what Latent flags is a real error.

**3. Checking every answer instead of a sample**\
Our classifier costs over 500x less than an LLM judge, so you can run it on all of your traffic. That catches 4x more hallucinations than checking a sample.

**4. Getting sharper on your data**\
Every answer your team confirms or clears becomes a label, so Latent calibrates to your traffic and improves the more you use it.

**5. Fitting into your stack**\
\`pip install runlatent\` wraps the model calls you already make, or you can point traffic at our OpenAI-compatible gateway. Self-hosted models run it as a vLLM plugin. Use it hosted, or run everything in your own cloud with nothing leaving your environment.

**The team:**

I'm a solo founder. At Penn (M&T), I published interpretability research at ACL, EMNLP, and NeurIPS on what a model's internals reveal that its outputs don't. Latent is the production version of that work. Before this, I worked on post-training at Amazon and Robinhood.

**Asks:**

If this sounds like your stack, I'd love to work with you. Reach out if you're:

* Running long-running agents, where one bad step early can derail everything after it.
* Doing research or continual learning, and want a signal the moment a model starts going wrong.
* Shipping AI in healthcare, finance, insurance, legal, or anywhere else a wrong answer is expensive.

**TL;DR:** We put robot arms into existing factories to automate repetitive work: machine tending, packing, and palletizing. They fit into the line you already have and adapt as your work changes.

Hi! We are [Alper](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alper-sametoglu) and [Samriddhi](https://linkedin.com/in/samriddhi-simi-s-1240321b5/), co-founders at [Odin Robotics](https://odin-robotics.com/).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-Mein4nAlA>

**Why the work stays manual** 

Traditional automation means rebuilding the factory around the robot. It's built for one product running the same way millions of times. Most factories don't work like that. They run many products, change over often, and handle parts that never show up exactly the same way twice. Robots that only follow a fixed program break the moment anything changes, so the work stays manual.

**What's in the demos**

* **Machine tending:** fully automated tending of a CNC mill. The robot loads raw parts, runs the cycle and unloads finished parts, with no operator needed.
* **Conveyor packing:** food containers picked off a moving conveyor and packed into totes in real time.

**Our approach** 

The best software combines deterministic code, trained models, and LLMs. Robotics is no different. Programmed controls run the steps that must be exact every time: machine doors, fixtures, safety zones. Learned skills handle everything that varies: new parts, mixed products, cluttered bins, and items that are soft or irregular. Our robots don't need every part perfectly placed. They handle the real variation of a working factory. Every deployment adds reusable skills and machine integrations, so each new factory goes live faster than the last.

**How to work with us**

1. **Show us the job:** the task, a photo or video of the setup, and current volume.
2. **We scope it:** scope, price, timeline, and safety guardrails, agreed up front.
3. **We deliver the full setup:** robot, end effector, sensors, and integration, installed on the existing line.

**Team**

Simi founded GirlsCanCode at 13 and grew it into a government-funded program. She has worked on robots ranging from humanoids to industrial arms, and left Electrical Engineering at ETH Zurich to build Odin.

Alper worked at a manufacturing intelligence startup in high school, built supersonic rockets and satellite propulsion valves, then turned down NASA JPL to deploy robots on Earth.

**Our ask:** Run or know a factory with repetitive loading, packing, or palletizing work? 

Send us the job, and we'll show you how it can be automated 📩 [**founders@odin-robotics.com**](mailto:founders@odin-robotics.com)

We’ve been building agentic systems for years (6 years to be exact…before it was cool), including really large ones that helped run major workflows inside Amazon. We know firsthand that the hard part isn’t getting an agent to work, it’s keeping it working at a high quality bar. We consistently saw that every model update and every prompt change shifted behavior in ways nobody caught until something downstream looked wrong. The only way to find out what changed was to pull traces and read them by hand.

Most companies shipping agents today are focused on the next feature for customers and they don't have time to fully maintain what's already been released. When we built our own agent as a three-person team, we hit the same wall. We needed to make sure our agent had high quality answers, was fast for our customers, and as low cost as possible, but we had to look at everything by hand. Every hour we spent examining traces was an hour we couldn’t spend on new product development. That's why we built Papaya.

At Papaya, our goal is to do the hard AI engineering work for you, staying up to date on the latest and greatest research so you can take advantage of this knowledge through optimizations. Simply stream your production traces through a lightweight SDK. From there, Papaya:

Thilo and I worked together at BCG, interviewing employees and repeatedly going back to them during implementation. On our evening runs, we started asking whether AI could make those conversations possible across an entire company.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every major decision depends on context. Much of it sits with employees who know how work happens and why things fail, but that knowledge rarely reaches the people deciding what to change.

We’re building Sona8 into the operating system for strategy and transformation teams. We will combine what our voice agents learn from employees with company data to build a live model of the organization. Teams will use it to compare alternatives and understand what a decision would require across sites and departments.

The same model will be the context layer for AI automation. Sona8 will use it to deploy agents and coordinate execution, then learn from the results. Small teams will be able to steer company-wide change, with the organization keeping what it learns as people and agents move on.

At BCG and McKinsey we often interviewed a few dozen people, hired interpreters and came back with a deck. The processes that were written down were never the lived processes and a few dozen interviews never gave us the full picture.\

* **Choose what you want to improve or automate.** Pick a question and the people to survey. This could be about sales quoting or mapping processes before implementing AI.

* **Use the findings and check progress.** See themes across interviews by department, get process maps, and ask again later to see what changed.

\

We’ve completed more than 10,000 employee interviews and signed one of the top three consulting firms.\
\
**Where this is going** \
Companies will try a lot of AI agents and automation tools in the next few years. Each one needs to know how the work is done before it changes anything, and most of that isn't written down. Sona8 creates infrastructure for AI automation tools. Over time we are building a live context graph of workflows by reading the systems a company already uses and connecting them to what employees say. \
\
**Who it’s for**\
Sona8 is for corporate development and transformation teams in enterprises, and the consulting firms supporting them. Reach out if you want to understand and improve how work gets done, roll out AI, or build AI tools that understand real-world workflows.\

name: Acyclic Labs
long_description:
Acyclic builds the infrastructure for agent swarms: open-source primitives for running agents in parallel, and a managed agents platform that runs swarms for you. Complex, long-running tasks are split across many agents, each working in its own instant fork of the workspace, and finish in a fraction of the time.

We built Acyclic because we believe there are huge gains to be had in how agents are run, beyond the models themselves. Agents can already do real work, but they still do it one step at a time, so complex tasks take hours or days. Running them as swarms is an infrastructure problem: isolating each agent, dividing the work, and merging the results without conflicts. Today, teams use Acyclic to run heavy document-processing pipelines in minutes instead of hours.

At Cambridge, we researched ML and auto-parallelising compilers, and then we built multi-agent systems in production: Ram as a Palantir FDE for pharma clients, shipping systems for clinical trial design, and Varun leading agent architecture at Tracelight for Big 4 accounting firms. We kept asking the same question: the agents were good enough, so why couldn't we run thousands of them at once to make everything faster and cheaper? Acyclic is our answer.
one_liner: Agent swarms that make long-running tasks exponentially faster

Markets move fast and in seemingly inexplicable ways, and opportunities disappear faster. Billionaires solve this problem by having family offices and teams of professionals that monitor both their existing portfolio and new opportunities closely. Most importantly, the professionals do this without prompting and come to their clients with personalized solutions. name: Hundred
long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up consumer devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm cosmetic defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

In the consumer electronics industry, designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

Hi, I’m [Melanie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/-melaniechen-/?isSelfProfile=true) and I’m the founder of[ Kiwi](https://withkiwi.ai/). 

<https://withkiwi.ai/> | [linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kiwi-ai-inc/) | [x/twitter](https://x.com/with_kiwi_ai)

### Tl;dr

Kiwi makes GTM agents self-improving and accurate, without having to hire data engineers. Every agent run can cite the SQL query it ran over the GTM data lake as evidence, and every decision or approval in the agent workflow powers evals that improve the agent. 

If you or another GTM team that you know is struggling to use agents in their day-to-day workflows and keeps falling back to repetitive, manual tasks, [trykiwi.now](http://trykiwi.now). 

<https://youtu.be/xozh9X5Hkd8>

### The problem

6 months ago, I was leading the post-sales team at a startup, and I hit a breaking point. I had spent 20 hours that week reviewing and fixing the work that my GTM teams’ agents had done. Despite spending hours each week on enablement, I always felt behind. Every week, the industry was moving forward with some new technique to best use agents efficiently and effectively, but onboarding the entire GTM organization onto a new workflow each week was impossible. On top of that, even when everyone had migrated to the new workflow, their agents were still generating slop because the underlying data wasn’t correct, and there was no way to ask the agents to show their work on each run. I started talking to other GTM teams, and now after learning from over 100 different companies, I’ve learned that there are two main obstacles keeping most GTM teams from becoming successfully agentic: 

1. Continuous enablement: Teams can easily adopt one skill, but as soon as operators fork the skills or context, it gets impossible to audit who’s using what agents where and for what and how successfully, or to push new changes to everyone’s agents. 
2. The data: when the underlying data infrastructure doesn’t exist, there is no way that agents can know how and where to fetch the data they need for a workflow.

### Kiwi handles the continuous enablement and maintenance of agents, as well as the data engineering, for you.

At Kiwi, we believe that an agent is only as good as the data that you give it. So, we sync all of the data from the tools in your GTM tool stack into a data lake. When you build an agent on Kiwi, we break it down into agent steps and human checkpoints, and every agent step that requires external data will show the SQL query that the agent runs under the hood, as well as a snapshot of the data pulled. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124027&key=user_uploads/1678005/27c31990-4696-41f4-b615-1ce6f5042a82)

Every checkpoint approval, feedback, or decline is also stored in the data lake, in addition to agent run parameters, so that Kiwi can detect shifts in your agent usage and suggest improvements. In addition, you can test agent changes against the data from historical runs. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124027&key=user_uploads/1678005/dea0699c-9987-4995-aa2d-7ec7da0f0d06)

With Kiwi, your GTM team can become fully AI-native without having to hire even more cooks in the kitchen or build out more surface area for your team to maintain. 

### Why us

The Kiwi team has spent years building data infrastructure that has powered billions of ACH and debit transactions at companies like Plaid, Jane Street, and Chalk, and experienced the pains of enablement firsthand. We’re building the platform that we wish we had, and could not find on the market. 

### Our Ask

If you or someone you know is struggling with how to make their GTM teams AI-native, we’d love an introduction! Reach out at [trykiwi.now](http://trykiwi.now), or email me at [melanie@withkiwi.ai](mailto:melanie@withkiwi.ai) !

We built and successfully hot-fired our first engine in 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 and have signed reservation agreements worth $𝟰𝟬𝟬𝗠. Now we are printing an engine with 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝘅 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 for a hot fire in November. If you’re a satellite operator, [reach out to us asap](https://calendar.app.google/xPzyR7iHmEJ3Gt116)**.**

<https://youtu.be/i-RuldD2YHU>	

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺

Satellite operators need to put more mass into orbit than ever, but an available launch slot can be 𝟯–𝟰 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 and cost up to $𝟭𝟱,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺. Every delay pushes back the start of operations and revenue.

As satellite constellations grow and new projects like space stations and orbital data centers take shape, customers need more launch capacity and more options.

As one European launch broker put it: “𝗜𝘁’𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝘀𝗹𝗼𝘁.”

𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

We’re building 𝗿𝗲𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝘃𝘆-𝗹𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗿𝘆 𝗽𝗮𝘆𝗹𝗼𝗮𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘂𝗽 𝘁𝗼 𝟮𝟬 𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝘀, powered by an engine architecture that aims to use 𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 than conventional designs.

We’ve 𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗺𝗽 by using a different method to pressurize the propellants and developed a **new rocket engine cycle** around it.

This simpler architecture reduces manufacturing complexity and cost, while reusability spreads the cost of the hardware across multiple flights.

Think of it as a 𝗯𝘂𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲: customers book capacity on a shared flight and pay by the kilogram.

Hi everyone, we’re Maria and Ary, founders of [Maritime](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/38061) (YC F26).

**TL;DR:** Maritime is a fully managed cloud platform for running millions of AI agents, each on its own isolated, persistent VM.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TnGXH9H0cTw>

**Why we built Maritime** 

We believe we’re heading toward a world with billions of AI agents. Everyone will have agents working for them, and businesses will run entire teams of AI employees. A new generation of startups will build and sell these agents, giving every customer one of their own.

We started working on Maritime when OpenClaw was released. Now, with dots, Instinct, Grok Bot, and Muse, that future is taking shape. We saw the infrastructure challenge firsthand while hosting hundreds of agents during our research at MIT. Even at that scale, our time went into getting environments running, maintaining them, and debugging individual agents.

Running billions of agents will require infrastructure that lets developers give each one a persistent computer and manage entire fleets with ease. We’re building Maritime to make that possible, so any startup can launch an agent product, give every customer their own agent, and scale it to millions in no time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120824&key=user_uploads/3118952/6772cfd5-737c-4278-8a02-ec3793cb070b)

**What Maritime does**

Maritime gives every agent a persistent computer and manages the infrastructure around it:

* **An isolated VM for each agent.** Run code, install software, and use a browser.
* **Pricing built for scale.** Hosting starts at $1 per agent per month, making it practical to give every customer their own persistent computer and grow your fleet as your product grows.
* **Persistence between tasks.** Keep files, memory, installed software, and logins so agents can pick up where they left off.
* **Tools to manage individual agents.** Inspect, debug, and fix each customer’s agent directly.
* **Different environments for different workflows.** Choose Linux computers, Windows desktops, or virtual Android phones based on the software and apps your agents need.

You can run your agent code inside a Maritime VM, or keep your agent on your existing backend and use MCP to let it control a Maritime computer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120824&key=user_uploads/3118952/db071ab8-94f8-4245-9de8-f574cc2aba1d)

**Who it’s for**

Teams building and selling AI employees, personal assistants, and other products where every customer has an agent of their own.

We want founders to focus on building and growing their products, with Maritime managing the infrastructure to run them.

**Our ask**

* **Try Maritime:** Host three agents for free at [maritime.sh](http://maritime.sh). Hosting starts at $1 per agent per month.

One of the biggest priorities of the department of war is energy dominance. We're seeing it constantly in new solicitations. Our strategy is superior - become a prime, but simultaneously service primes because most of then don't actually have the battery and power electronics expertise we have.

launches.title: DeepMark - Reinventing Trust in Voice
launches.tagline: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/76SqazbxK4w>

Hey, we are Slavko and Kosta 👋

We have been working together for six years, first as two researchers at the University of Montenegro, now as founders. Somewhere along the way, we became best friends. Kosta is our CSO, and I am the CEO.

**The problem**

Voice is uniquely vulnerable to impersonation. A few seconds of audio is enough to clone anyone, and the same voice agents that answer a bank's phone can be turned around and pointed at the bank's customers. People have started to hesitate before picking up. Good technology scales good outcomes, and it scales bad ones just as well. Our job is simple. Restore trust in voice.

**What we built**

DeepMark is real-time audio watermarking for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we put a certificate inside the sound itself, on the voice company's side, as the voice is being generated. Not metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The certificate becomes part of the voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/b3239118-82c1-4fb4-82c2-f4363685a0be)

Then the voice goes out into the real world, and the real world is rough on audio. Compression, codecs, a bad connection, a cheap speaker, a worse microphone. Think about how flat a human voice sounds over the phone. Our certificate survives the trip. On the other end, a phone, a call center, or an API reads it and shows who is speaking, who issued the certificate, and whether this agent is allowed to be on the line. Detectors ask whether audio is fake. We answer who is authorized to speak.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/171abdf5-efb9-442b-a153-dbbb1ba981d4)

**Why this is hard**

Four things have to hold at the same time. It has to be real time, or a phone call makes no sense, and voice companies already fight for every millisecond. It has to leave the audio quality alone, nobody trades a worse voice for a safer one. It has to survive the phone line. And the ID has to be long enough, because the longer the ID, the more certificates we can issue. A watermark that works beautifully in the lab falls apart the moment audio meets a phone line. And a live call has no file to sign. Nothing survives the trip except the sound itself, so the identity has to live inside the sound. We spent years hitting that wall. Then we built a tool that measures all four at once and published it, so anyone can check our work, and everyone else's.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/a9930538-1deb-4609-8938-4bdbcf8c88ce)

**How we got here**

Our mentor, who did his PhD in digital watermarking, told us not to bother. The field was saturated, nothing left to contribute. We were too stubborn to listen, and our learning-based approach turned out to be one of the first of its kind.

Kosta wrote his PhD on watermarking along the way. I am still writing mine! We published some of the earliest work in deep audio watermarking, cited by teams at Meta, Microsoft, Sony, and Adobe. This year our robustness benchmark landed in IEEE Access, and our AWARE paper was accepted at EUSIPCO. Before YC, we signed our first platform license with a leading voice AI provider, and it is now in production.

**Our ask**

We want to meet voice AI companies. If you build voice models, book 20 minutes with us and we will run DeepMark on your own audio, so you can see the mark survive your calls. The EU AI Act's marking rules already apply and the 2 December deadline for systems on the market is close, so this is a good month to talk. If you know someone at a voice AI platform, an intro means a lot to us.

[slavko@deepmark.me](mailto:slavko@deepmark.me), or book a demo at [deepmark.me](http://deepmark.me). Thanks for reading. 🇲🇪 → 🌉

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Every healthcare transaction should be paid according to the contract. Today, billions aren't. Cesara reads a health system's payer contracts and checks every claim against them when it's submitted. When a payment comes back short, Cesara automatically files the appeal with the contract clause attached and recovers the money. \
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IDbQo3WsSGY>

### The problem: contracts change, but team capacity doesn't

Payer contracts keep changing. Amendments, fee schedule updates and annual rate increases all change what a hospital should be paid partway through the year. Every change has to be loaded and checked by hand. Revenue cycle and managed care teams can't keep up, so underpayments only show up months later in spreadsheets, after the payment has posted. **Health systems lose $40B+ a year from contractual underpayments.**

### How Cesara works

* **Every contract in one place.** Cesara pulls rates, carve-outs, stop-loss terms and rate increases from the contracts themselves. It keeps them in sync with Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email and your chargemaster.
* **Every claim checked when it's submitted.** Cesara calculates the expected payment up front. Say a payer pays $42,000 on a claim where the contract's stop-loss clause means $78,000 is owed. Your team sees the gap right away, with the clause attached.
* **Automatic recovery.** Cesara files each appeal with the contract excerpt and the payer's remittance (835) attached. It tracks the appeal until the money is recovered and the claim is closed.
* **Better contract negotiations.** Your team can ask its contracts anything in plain language and model proposed rates before signing. They walk into payer meetings with payment trends and evidence ready.

### Enterprise grade from day one

Cesara is built for health systems, not retrofitted for them. It connects to Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email, Waystar and Availity, and it posts work to Teams and Slack.

* **Rolled out in phases.** Cesara first runs alongside your current process to prove its accuracy on your own claims. Next it recommends actions for your team to approve. Then it recovers underpayments automatically within limits you set.
* **Every action traceable.** Each underpayment, appeal and recovery links to the contract clause behind it, and every action is logged.
* **Your team reviews exceptions, not every claim.** Anything above your approval threshold goes to your team before Cesara acts on it.

Want a free audit of your claims? [**team@cesara.com**](mailto:team@cesara.com)

launches.body:
Hey everyone, I'm Michael, the founder of [Spacesheep](https://spacesheep.dev) (F26).

## TL;DR

**Spacesheep: documents of the future.** Spaces are the place your teams and agents can be productive. Your AI makes the space; your team reads it, comments on it and builds on it.

Ask the AI you already use: "Use spacesheep.dev and give a visual explanation of how GPUs work." You get a document, a mockup, a dashboard, an app or art. Share it with specific people, your team, or publicly.

Our launch video:

<https://youtu.be/cFVCDSs-GZs>

Agents make our work more productive. Their output keeps growing, but our ability to read stays the same. We're building a new surface where people understand and work with AI.

Spacesheep in 90 seconds:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKQtOTrRBBA>

## Why we're building it

Agent use pushes productivity, but we get constantly burned out by relentless walls of AI-generated text. We don't believe a chat interface is the final evolution of human-computer interaction. Agents know how to shape information for humans, and that shape is not a wall of text. The full story: [spacesheep.dev/why](https://spacesheep.dev/why)

## What we built

If you can imagine it, you can sheep it. Information can take many more shapes than a page. With one prompt, create and share designs, styled documents, dashboards and vibe-coded apps your team and customers work in together.

### Dashboards and live data

Cited, charted, and kept current. Machines and services stream numbers straight into the space, like [a thermal camera on an AI chip's board](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/thermal-master-p3-live-camera-stream) at 25 frames a second while GPU experiments run, or [an AI Foundry lab dashboard](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/aifoundry-lab-dashboard).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/70f6f951-c043-4261-af2a-4379d7cfed7c)


### Investigations

Turn agent output into dashboards and stories people actually understand. For example, [YC by the numbers](https://spacesheep.dev/@misha/yc-by-the-numbers): we pointed an agent at YC's public directory, 6,305 startups over 21 years, and it came back as one story in six eras, from consumer web to agents and robots.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/74805160-58ea-40a9-b983-15b2d92b1491)


### Interactive designs

[An interactive map of the ET-SoC-1 chip](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/et-soc1-chip-diagram) you can click through and comment on, from the whole chip down to a single vector unit. Each space is designed from scratch for what's in it. No templates.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/c7047d56-9b60-4933-a50c-97fe3927c356)


### Apps, CRMs and forms

Teams build their own internal apps, CRMs and forms, even games: for productivity, for fun, or for working with suppliers and customers. Everyone edits the same records, and there are no servers to run.

### Collaborate

Jump on a space with your team and your AI. Comment on the exact line. Write @spacesheep and the AI fixes the space while everyone watches. Every version is kept.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/e1e00c9c-53c7-4a5b-873e-a8e58e31dba4)


This is how James Briggs uses it to stay in the loop while Claude Code writes his code: plans, code explainers and reviews he can actually read.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJVcc4O-7ck>

### Never lose a link

Ask in your own words and the space is there. State-of-the-art search, built by former Pinecone engineers.

### Use your AI. Or ours.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok and open-source harnesses like opencode all publish to the same space. Or use Spacesheep's own AI on the dashboard, in Slack and more.

### Own your data

Your spaces are yours. Every space and every version syncs to your own Google Drive or GitHub, so you can read them anywhere, take them with you, and never depend on us to keep them.

## About me

Founder/CEO of Spacesheep (YC F26). Previously MTS at Anthropic, where I built the internal app deployment framework and the first version of CC Artifacts. Before that, staff engineer at Pinecone and Twitter.

## Our ask

* **Try it.** Ask your agent to "share this to spacesheep.dev" and send the link to your team.
* **Design partners.** Know an organization that wants to use Spacesheep? Introduce us.
* **Feedback:** [feedback@spacesheep.dev](mailto:feedback@spacesheep.dev) or [@micmakarov](https://x.com/micmakarov) on X
* **YC founders:** a year of the Team plan for up to 15 members. Redeem it on Bookface.
